info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package patent is the record of who thought of what, and when the machine was asked to write it.

get.summary: Returns the decision trail — each person's current word on each disclosure.
get.description:
Returns the decision trail — each person's current word on
each disclosure. ?disclosure= narrows to one document.

parameters.name: disclosure
parameters.description: Disclosure narrows to the decisions on one document.

post.summary: Appends one person's decision about one disclosure.
post.description:
Appends one person's decision about one disclosure. The
approver is the validated principal and nothing else, so no caller records a
sign-off on someone else's behalf — which is the only way this field would be
worth reading.

approvals.comment: research log reviewed, the mechanism is ours

get.summary: Returns the canonical disclosures, each carrying its current approvals.
get.description:
Returns the canonical disclosures, each carrying its
current approvals.

post.summary: Appends the assembled document and the record ids it rests on.
post.description:
Appends the assembled document and the record ids it
rests on. The document is a rendering of what the log already holds, and its
citations are what let a reader check it instead of taking it.

post.summary: Makes the decision a recording never implied: whether an idea, implementation or disclosure stays private to its author's project, opens to the org, or goes public.
post.description:
Makes the decision a recording never implied: whether an
idea, implementation or disclosure stays private to its author's project, opens
to the org, or goes public. Publication of a conception entry is a
disclosure under 35 U.S.C. §102 in every jurisdiction that reads it that way,
so it is always a separate call and never a side effect of writing one down.

get.summary: Reports what this deployment actually guarantees about the records it keeps, in honest states.
get.description:
Reports what this deployment actually guarantees about the
records it keeps, in honest states. Anchored and durable are the two that
change what a record is worth, and an unwired one reads as unwired rather than
as a green light.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's canonical conception entries, oldest appended first, which is the order the log says they were thought.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's canonical conception entries, oldest
appended first, which is the order the log says they were thought. ?id= narrows
to one, ?kind= to one kind, ?project= to one project.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
ID reads one entry, which is how a single idea is addressed — there is no
second route for it.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Kind narrows to one kind of conception entry.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Project narrows to one project; empty reads the org's whole set.

post.description:
Appends conception entries. A write states the idea and
nothing else: the project, the author, the clock, the append order and the
content digest are all the server's, and a correction appends a version rather
than editing the entry — which is the property that makes any of it usable as
evidence at all.

get.summary: Returns the canonical implementation records with their citations.
get.description:
Returns the canonical implementation records with
their citations. ?idea= is the query the record exists to answer: which
artifacts rest on this one conception entry.

parameters.name: idea
parameters.description:
Idea narrows to implementations citing one conception entry — which is
how a correction finds every artifact built on the idea it invalidates.

post.summary: Appends the machine's half of the record, and the idea citation is the load-bearing field: it is what lets a reader see that the conception came first.
post.description:
Appends the machine's half of the record, and the
idea citation is the load-bearing field: it is what lets a reader see that the
conception came first. An entry citing no idea is refused rather than filed.

get.summary: Folds the caller's record set and answers the ordering question over it.
get.description:
Folds the caller's record set and answers the ordering question
over it.

?disclosure= proves one document's set, ?idea= proves one entry and everything
citing it, and neither proves the whole org. The answer is computed per request
and writes nothing.

parameters.name: disclosure
parameters.description:
Disclosure folds the record set one document rests on, and reports on
that set alone — which is what an attorney asks for.

parameters.name: idea
parameters.description: Idea narrows to the one entry and the artifacts citing it.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Project narrows inside the org; empty reads the caller's scope.

get.summary: Returns every retained version of one entry, in append order.
get.description:
Returns every retained version of one entry, in append
order. ?id= names it and ?kind= says which log; a retraction is shown as the
withdrawal it is rather than hidden.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the entry's stable id. Required.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Kind is idea, implementation or disclosure — which log to read.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Project narrows inside the org; empty is the caller's own scope.

at.description: At is when the commitment was made, RFC3339, when there is one.

commitment.description: Commitment is the fold root the anchor would name.

reference.description:
Reference is where a third party can check it — a block, an index, a
published headline. Empty means nothing outside this response names it.

status.description:
Status is unanchored or anchored. Nothing else: an anchored answer arrives
only from a real commitment, and this app never invents a transaction id.

authored_by.description:
AuthoredBy is the validated principal who decided. The same rule as
everywhere here: it comes from the credential, never the body, so one
person cannot record a decision on another's behalf.

canonical.description:
Canonical is DERIVED on read: this author's latest word on this
disclosure.

comment.description: Comment is the reviewer's note — the part an inventor reads.

content_hash.description: ContentHash is the server's digest of the recorded content.

decision.description:
Decision is approved, rejected or needs-work. A needs-work is dated and
retained exactly like a sign-off, because it IS one.

disclosure_id.description: DisclosureID is the document this decides on. Required.

id.description:
ID is the server's handle for this decision, derived from the disclosure
and its author. Read-only: a caller cannot name someone else's approval.

project.description: Project is the SERVER's scope value.

revision.description: Revision is original, corrected or retracted.

role.description:
Role is the capacity the person acted in: author, cto, reviewer, attorney
or counsel. Required, because "approved" by nobody is not a fact.

approvals.description: Approvals is how many decisions it covered.

disclosures.description: Disclosures is how many documents it covered.

ideas.description: Ideas is how many conception entries the fold covered.

implementations.description: Implementations is how many implementation records it covered.

versions.description:
Versions is how many RETAINED versions were folded, which is at least the
sum above and is the number that says corrections happened.

approvals.description:
Approvals is DERIVED on read: the current decision of record from each
person who has ruled on this disclosure. Never an input — a caller cannot
approve its own document by writing a field in it.

authored_by.description: AuthoredBy is the validated principal who recorded this version.

body.description:
Body is the document's text. Its digest is published beside it so a reader
can tell a stored body from a re-sent one.

body_sha256.description:
BodySHA256 is the SERVER's digest of body. On a read it is the address of
what is stored; a body is never hashed from what a reader sent.

claims.description: Claims is the draft claim set, or a pointer to where it lives.

content_hash.description: ContentHash is the server's digest of the recorded content.

filing_ref.description:
FilingRef is a filing number a human recorded here after filing. Empty
means nothing has been filed, and no code path fills it.

id.description: ID is the disclosure's stable id. Required.

idea_ids.description:
IdeaIDs are the conception entries this disclosure is built from. The
evidence half; a disclosure citing none is an assertion.

implementation_ids.description: ImplementationIDs are the artifacts it describes.

project.description: Project is the SERVER's scope value.

revision.description: Revision is original, corrected or retracted.

status.description:
Status is draft, reviewed, approved or filed. `approved` means the
approvals below carry a decision for each required role, which is DERIVED
on read, not a word a caller sets and gets believed.

summary.description:
Summary is the invention in one paragraph, for the reader who decides
whether to read the rest.

title.description: Title names the invention the way the document does.

visibility.description: Visibility is private, org or public; forced private on a write.

field.description: Field is the wire name, e.g. prior_art.

missing.description: Missing is how many covered records leave it empty.

why.description:
Why names what the absence costs, so a gap is a decision to fix rather
than a lint warning.

alternatives.description: Alternatives are the routes considered and rejected, each with its reason.

authored_by.description:
AuthoredBy is the validated principal who recorded this version — an IAM
subject, never a body field. It is the §115 answer, and a model has none.

canonical.description:
Canonical is DERIVED on read: a version is canonical when it is the
latest-appended non-retracted version of its id.

content_hash.description:
ContentHash is the SERVER's digest of the recorded content and this
version's identity. Computed on a write; read back on a read.

id.description:
ID is the entry's stable id, the key its versions accrue under:
lowercase, terse, and named for the idea rather than the file —
latency-aware-request-routing. Required on a write.

kind.description:
Kind is what kind of conception this is: problem, alternative,
architecture, mechanism, decision or rejection. Required on a write.

notes.description: Notes is anything a later reader needs that the fields above cannot carry.

prior_art.description:
PriorArt is what the author knows already existed, named as the author
knows it. It is a statement of the inventor's awareness, not a search
result, and it is not a substitute for one.

problem.description:
Problem is the technical problem being solved, and why the existing
approaches fail at it.

project.description:
Project is the sub-scope inside the org this entry is filed under. On a
write it is the SERVER's value and a project in the body is ignored.

recorded_at.description:
RecordedAt is when this store accepted the version, RFC3339, from the
server clock.

revision.description:
Revision is the producer's declared kind of this version: original,
corrected or retracted. A retracted latest version WITHDRAWS the id; every
earlier version stays retained.

seq.description:
Seq is this version's place in the store's append order. The ordering
authority; never a client value.

signature.description: PatentSignature is an optional detached signature over this entry's digest.

statement.description:
Statement is the operative idea in the author's own prose — definite
enough that a reader could implement it from this alone. Required, and the
field an examiner would actually read.

title.description: Title is the one-line name of the entry.

visibility.description: Visibility is private, org or public. A write forces private.

artifact_sha256.description:
ArtifactSHA256 is the digest of the recorded artifact — a diff, a file, a
build — when the caller has one and wants it addressed by content.

authored_by.description:
AuthoredBy is the validated principal who recorded this. Authorship of the
IDEA is PatentIdea.AuthoredBy — this field records who filed the
implementation record, which is not the same question.

content_hash.description: ContentHash is the server's digest of the recorded content.

generated.description:
Generated says the recorded artifact was produced with a model's
assistance rather than typed by hand.

git_branch.description: GitBranch is the branch that commit was on.

git_dirty.description:
GitDirty says the working tree carried uncommitted changes when this was
recorded. It is recorded because an exact commit claim that is not true is
worse than no commit claim.

git_sha.description:
GitSHA is the commit. Together with Seq it is what makes the claim checkable
outside this app: a reader can go read the code.

human_review.description:
HumanReview is what a person did with the output: accepted, edited,
rewritten, or none. `none` on a novel mechanism is the disposition to
know about.

id.description:
ID is this implementation's stable id — usually the artifact or change it
records, e.g. router-v2-generated. Required.

idea_ids.description:
IdeaIDs names the conceptions this implements. REQUIRED and non-empty:
an implementation citing nothing is the inverted order the guidance is
written against, and filing it silently would be the worst thing this
surface could do.

model.description:
Model names the system that produced the code, as it was addressed. This is
the field that answers "how much of this was a tool" without a guess.

notes.description: Notes is anything a later reader needs.

project.description: Project is the SERVER's scope value.

prompt_sha256.description:
PromptSHA256 is the digest of the prompt, not the prompt. The text often
carries third-party material; the digest lets a later reader prove the
same request was made.

repo.description: Repo is the repository the work landed in.

revision.description: Revision is original, corrected or retracted.

seq.description:
Seq is the append order, which is what GET /v1/patent/proof compares
against the cited ideas.

visibility.description: Visibility is private, org or public; forced private on a write.

gap_seq.description:
GapSeq is how many appends separate them, negative when the implementation
precedes the idea. It is a distance in the LOG rather than in seconds,
because seconds are comparable only within one server's clock.

idea.description: Idea is the conception it cites.

implementation.description: Implementation is the artifact being examined.

verdict.description: Verdict is before, after or unproven.

why.description:
Why states, in one sentence, what the verdict is resting on. A verdict
without its basis is the thing this whole surface exists to avoid.

anchor.description: PatentAnchor is the external standing of this exact root.

coverage.description:
Coverage counts what the fold held, per kind, so a short list reads as a
short log and not as a complete one.

gaps.description:
Gaps names every field of the covered records that states nothing, with
how many records leave it unstated.

order.description: Order is one verdict per implementation-idea pair.

project.description: Project is the scope the fold covered.

records.description: Records are the entries folded, oldest clock first.

root.description: Root is the fold digest over every record in append order.

verdict.description:
Verdict is the whole answer in one word: supported when every pair is
`before`, contested when any is `after`, unproven when any is missing, and
empty when there was nothing to fold. It is the WORST pair, because a chain
with one inverted edge is not a chain.

verified_at.description:
VerifiedAt is when this fold was computed. The records can have grown since;
the root is the set as of here.

authored_by.description: AuthoredBy is the validated subject on the record.

content_hash.description: ContentHash is the server's digest of the recorded content.

digest.description:
Digest is what the fold consumed: content hash and clock together, so two
versions of one id with identical content still differ in the fold.

id.description: ID is the record's stable id.

kind.description: Kind is idea, implementation, disclosure or approval.

recorded_at.description: RecordedAt is the server clock at the append.

revision.description: Revision is original, corrected or retracted.

seq.description: Seq is the append clock value. The ordering authority.

option.description: Option is the approach, in the author's words.

reason.description: Reason is why it was rejected — the constraint or failure that decided it.

algo.description: Algo names the scheme, e.g. ed25519. Empty means the record does not say.

key_id.description: KeyID names the key that signed. It is a reference, not public bytes.

verified.description:
Verified is the SERVER's answer to whether it checked this signature. It is
false on a deployment with no verifier wired, and a record carrying an
unchecked signature says so rather than borrowing credibility.

found.description: Found is false when no version of that id exists in this org.

kind.description: Kind is which log was read.

project.description: Project is the scope it is filed under.

versions.description: Versions are every retained version, oldest append first.

authored_by.description: AuthoredBy is the validated subject who appended it.

canonical.description:
Canonical marks the version a listing would return: the latest non-retracted
one. Exactly one entry per id is canonical, or none, when the latest retracts.

recorded_at.description: RecordedAt is the server clock at the append.

revision.description: Revision is original, corrected or retracted.

seq.description: Seq is the append clock value this version was stamped with.

superseded.description:
Superseded marks a retained version that a later one replaced. Retained and
superseded are both true of most of a long history, and that is the point.

approvals.description: Approvals are the decisions to append, at most 2000.

data.description: Data are the current decisions of record, oldest append first.

disclosures.description: Disclosures are the documents to append, at most 2000.

data.description: Data are the canonical disclosures, oldest append first.

id.description: ID is the record's stable id.

kind.description: Kind is idea, implementation or disclosure — what the id names.

project.description: Project locates the record inside the caller's own org.

visibility.description: Visibility is private, org or public.

ideas.description: Ideas are the entries to append, at most 2000.

data.description: Data are the canonical entries, oldest append first.

implementations.description: Implementations are the records to append, at most 2000.

data.description: Data are the canonical records, oldest append first.

updated.description:
Updated is how many records the grant moved to the visibility asked for.
It counts every RETAINED version of the target, so it is at least one.

anchored.description:
Anchored is whether record roots are committed outside this platform.
False is the common case and the important one: without it the chain
proves order WITHIN the platform's own honesty and nothing beyond it.

durable.description:
Durable is whether acknowledged writes are fenced to a durable object.
False means a store is local to this pod: the records stand, failover does
not carry them.

now.description:
RecordedAt is the server's time now, RFC3339 — so a reader can tell how
stale its own view is.

signature_verification.description:
SignatureVerification is whether the server can verify a submitted
detached signature. Attribution does not depend on it — the author of
every record is the validated principal, never a body field — but a
record carrying a signature it cannot check says so.

stamped_by.description:
ServerClockSays is what stamps a record: always "server", because no
client-supplied timestamp is read anywhere in this package.

canonical.description: Canonical is how many entries the org's log now holds for this kind.

project.description: Project is the scope the batch was filed under, as the server decided it.

recorded.description: Recorded is how many new versions this call appended.

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
